subject.title: cron: reject webhook URLs with embedded credentials

question: Should cron webhook URL userinfo be rejected fail-closed for existing stored jobs, or must this PR add a doctor/audit migration and compatibility proof first?
rationale: Rejecting URL userinfo reduces secret exposure, but it also changes existing stored cron delivery behavior and may stop callbacks after upgrade; automation should not decide that security/compatibility tradeoff without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require upgrade path before merge
options.body: Add doctor/audit handling, redacted warnings, focused tests, and real cron-path proof before accepting the stricter validator.

options.title: Accept fail-closed hardening
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept breaking credentialed webhook URLs as a security boundary, but the PR should document that decision and prove the runtime warning path.

options.title: Replace with redaction-first hardening
options.body: Close or supersede this branch with a narrower change that redacts credentialed URLs first while leaving delivery compatibility unchanged until a migration exists.

recommendation.title: Require upgrade path before merge
recommendation.body: Add doctor/audit handling, redacted warnings, focused tests, and real cron-path proof before accepting the stricter validator.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties Peter Steinberger to the current cron webhook helper, notification dispatch, and doctor migration code that must own the policy decision.
